first.rationale: Prioritize a targeted onboarding-simplification experiment because completion is down 4% QoQ and prior evidence indicates simplification improves completion, time-to-value, and early self-serve adoption. Verify the prior onboarding result and promotional-pricing retention tradeoff before commitment: competitor pricing creates urgency, but acquisition gains that erode retention would conflict with sustainable qualified revenue.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding for self-serve accounts. The verified prior result directly addresses the 4% QoQ completion decline and showed completion +13%, time-to-value reduced by 2.1 days, and 30-day retention +3%, supporting sustainable qualified revenue rather than only top-of-funnel volume. Do not use promotional pricing despite competitive pressure: its verified acquisition and qualified-revenue lift came with a 12% 30-day retention decline and failure to survive the first renewal cycle. Monitor activation recovery and retention by SMB segment, since prior results do not establish that onboarding changes alone will fully offset the competitor-driven loss of price-sensitive accounts.

final2.rationale: Keep the onboarding-simplification experiment. The deeper competitor cut and doubled price-related churn conversations increase urgency, but they do not overturn the verified evidence that promotional pricing produces an unsustainable cohort: +18% qualified revenue alongside -12% 30-day retention and failure before first renewal. Simplified onboarding remains the strongest verified response to the concurrent completion decline and supports durable value through higher completion, faster time-to-value, and +3% 30-day retention. The current churn signal may warrant a future retention-focused pricing investigation, but no evidence available this cycle establishes that discounts will retain the existing SMB base sustainably.
